name: Choose an appropriate metric unit
description: Student can choose an appropriate metric unit for measuring an attribute.
exampleOfSuccess: To measure a room, the student chooses metres rather than millimetres.
commonError: Student chooses a unit that is too small or too large for the task.
checkpointTask: Name things to measure. Ask the student which metric unit suits each.

name: Order metric units by size
description: Student can order metric units of an attribute from largest to smallest.
exampleOfSuccess: The student orders kilometre, metre, centimetre, millimetre.
commonError: Student mixes up the order, or muddles units of different attributes.
checkpointTask: Give metric units of length or mass. Ask the student to order them by size.

name: Use a smaller unit for accuracy
description: Student can use a smaller unit to obtain a more accurate measure.
exampleOfSuccess: The student measures in centimetres rather than metres for a more accurate length.
commonError: Student keeps a unit too large to capture the detail needed.
checkpointTask: Pose a measuring task needing precision. Ask the student which unit gives a better measure.

name: Use a combination of units
description: Student can record a measure using a combination of units.
exampleOfSuccess: The student records a height as 1 m 35 cm.
commonError: Student records only one unit, losing accuracy or meaning.
checkpointTask: Pose measures that span two units. Ask the student to record each.

name: Calculate the perimeter of a rectangle
description: Student can calculate the perimeter of a rectangle.
exampleOfSuccess: For a 6 m by 4 m rectangle, the student finds 20 m.
commonError: Student adds only two sides, or confuses perimeter with area.
checkpointTask: Give rectangles with labelled sides. Ask the student to find the perimeter.

name: Calculate the area of a rectangle
description: Student can calculate the area of a rectangle in square units.
exampleOfSuccess: For a 6 m by 4 m rectangle, the student finds 24 square metres.
commonError: Student adds the sides instead of multiplying for area.
checkpointTask: Give rectangles. Ask the student to find the area.

name: Find the perimeter of an irregular shape
description: Student can find the perimeter of an irregular shape by adding all sides.
exampleOfSuccess: The student adds every side of an L-shaped figure to find the perimeter.
commonError: Student misses a side, or includes an internal line.
checkpointTask: Give irregular shapes with labelled sides. Ask the student to find each perimeter.

name: Solve a practical area problem
description: Student can solve a practical problem involving area, such as floor covering.
exampleOfSuccess: The student finds how much carpet a room needs by calculating its area.
commonError: Student finds perimeter instead of area, or uses wrong units.
checkpointTask: Pose a practical area problem. Ask the student to solve it.

name: Convert 12-hour time to 24-hour time
description: Student can convert a time from 12-hour to 24-hour format.
commonError: Student adds 12 to am times, or leaves pm times unchanged.
checkpointTask: Give 12-hour times. Ask the student to write each in 24-hour time.

name: Convert 24-hour time to 12-hour time
description: Student can convert a time from 24-hour to 12-hour format.
commonError: Student subtracts 12 from morning times, or mislabels am and pm.
checkpointTask: Give 24-hour times. Ask the student to write each in 12-hour time.

name: Read a 24-hour timetable
description: Student can read and use a timetable written in 24-hour time.
exampleOfSuccess: The student reads a flight departing at 14:05 as leaving at 2:05 pm.
commonError: Student misreads the 24-hour times on the timetable.
checkpointTask: Give a 24-hour timetable. Ask the student to answer questions about it.

name: Solve a duration problem using 24-hour time
description: Student can solve a duration problem using 24-hour time.
exampleOfSuccess: From 13:20 to 15:05, the student finds 1 hour 45 minutes.
commonError: Student miscounts across the hour, or converts incorrectly.
checkpointTask: Pose duration problems in 24-hour time. Ask the student to solve each.

name: Measure an angle with a protractor
description: Student can measure an angle in degrees using a protractor.
exampleOfSuccess: The student measures an angle as 65 degrees, lining up the protractor correctly.
commonError: Student reads the wrong scale on the protractor, or misaligns the baseline.
checkpointTask: Give angles and a protractor. Ask the student to measure each.

name: Estimate the size of an angle in degrees
description: Student can estimate the size of an angle in degrees before measuring.
exampleOfSuccess: The student estimates an angle as about 90 degrees, then checks.
commonError: Student estimates with no reference to known angles like 90 degrees.
checkpointTask: Show angles. Ask the student to estimate each in degrees before measuring.

name: Classify an angle by its measure
description: Student can classify an angle by its degree measure.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says a 120 degree angle is obtuse.
commonError: Student names the angle type without regard to the measure.
checkpointTask: Give angle measures. Ask the student to name the type of each.

name: Construct an angle with a protractor
description: Student can construct an angle of a given size using a protractor.
exampleOfSuccess: The student constructs a 45 degree angle accurately.
commonError: Student draws the angle without measuring, or measures from the wrong line.
checkpointTask: Name angle sizes. Ask the student to construct each with a protractor.
